task: Retire six remaining lattice identities (two bin aliases, two state directories, two config filenames, one npm package name) that B-cdf6 deliberately left in place, migrating live on-disk state without orphaning or rewriting it.
outcome: proof-or-stop resolves all state, config and package identities under proof-or-stop names; the 344 archived story directories remain readable and their historical signatures still verify; no bare .lattice / lattice.config.json / @lattice/core literal remains in product runtime source.
facts: Measured in this worktree at PLAN time: git ls-files .lattice | wc -l = 7580 tracked files; ls .lattice/story/actives | wc -l = 344 story directories. Earlier counts of 7571/7574 and 326 were taken on main days apart; the numbers drift with ongoing story activity, so any acceptance check must re-measure rather than assert a literal.

The 8 lattice-*-integrity-v1 signature salts are standalone string constants (core/finding-verify.ts declares FINDING_SALT and REVIEW_PASS_SALT as literals; 6 siblings elsewhere). They are NOT derived from any directory or filename, so renaming paths does not invalidate historical signatures. Independently re-verified by the INIT reviewer.

docs/requirements/decisions/brand-rename-mapping.md:124 gives the .lattice/ state-directory NAME a verdict of RENAMED (additive); only the literal VALUE is frozen in a parenthetical. This story completes that prescribed path. An earlier draft of the background wrongly called it a FROZEN override; corrected after INIT-001.
.lattice/learning/ is explicitly materialHash-EXCLUDED (core/learning-store.ts, core/command-policy.ts), so cache churn there cannot make evidence stale.

B-cdf6 established the additive read-both pattern in core/brand-env.ts: canonical name wins, deprecated name still resolves. This story reuses that pattern for paths and filenames rather than inventing a new mechanism.

B-cdf6 lesson with direct bearing here: four regressions (F-061/F-065 at core/lattice-dispatch.ts:1671-1677 and 1702-1713, F-062 at core/done-required-timeout-budget.ts:178, F-068 at cli/activity-policy.ts:136) were hardcoded DEPRECATED literals inside comparisons and parsers, so the CANONICAL spelling silently failed while the old one worked. All four were found by reviewers, none by the implementer.

The canonical AST fingerprint for cli-engine.ts has TWO coupled pinned copies (tasks/retired-authority-vocabulary-guard-smoke.ts and scripts/verify-process-fact-contract.mjs); updating only one fails closed.

A fresh worktree needs THREE setup steps, not one: npm install at root, npm --prefix packages/main install + build, and npm --prefix packages/utils install + build. The packages/main build exits 0 while producing no dist when its own deps are missing, so exit code alone is not a build-success signal.
constraints: Never rewrite content inside archived story files. History MOVES (git mv preserves content and follows history); it is never edited.
The 8 signature salts and the 13 lattice-* agent role IDs are out of scope and must remain byte-identical (scope-boundary excludedScope).
Read-both must hold for every renamed identity: the deprecated path/filename stays READABLE while only the canonical name is WRITTEN. A teammate branch or unmigrated project must still load.
Deprecation notices go to STDERR, never stdout: B-cdf6 established that stdout contamination breaks --json for piped consumers.
CHK-003 (the git mv) must not start until CHK-008 (the apply-then-revert rehearsal) is done and its evidence recorded. ID order is not execution order in this story.
Removing the bin aliases (CHK-006) is the one irreversible break of B-cdf6 multi-developer compatibility guarantee, so it goes LAST and must be ANNOUNCED via CHANGELOG, not merely performed.
git push, npm publish, rm -rf on either state directory, and history-rewriting commands are blocked by execution-boundary.
unknowns: Whether storyFilesHash includes file PATHS or only content: if it hashes relative paths, the state-dir rename shifts it for every story and CHK-001 must decide whether that is acceptable drift or requires a rebind step. Must be resolved in CHK-001 before CHK-003 runs.
Whether any external consumer resolves @lattice/core from a registry; determines whether CHK-005 needs a deprecated alias package or is a clean break.
Whether .lattice-serve.json (runtime discovery, gitignored) has readers outside this repo that would break on rename.
